title: Severe choking
summary: Encourage an effective cough; for severe obstruction use cycles of 5 back blows and 5 thrusts.
sources: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care — Foreign-Body Airway Obstruction
actions: If the person can speak clearly and cough strongly, encourage coughing and watch closely.
For an adult or child older than 1 year who cannot speak, breathe, or cough effectively, call emergency services. Give 5 firm back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts; repeat.
In late pregnancy or when you cannot encircle the abdomen, use 5 chest thrusts instead of abdominal thrusts.
For an infant younger than 1 year, use 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts. Do not use abdominal thrusts.
If the person becomes unresponsive, lower them to a firm surface and start CPR with chest compressions. Before breaths, remove only an object you can clearly see. Use an AED when available.
prohibitions: Do not use a blind finger sweep.
Do not use abdominal thrusts on an infant.
Do not leave a person with severe obstruction alone.

emergencyCall.text: If the person cannot speak, breathe, or cough effectively, call emergency services now.
